correctness.rationale: Under the invertible congruence Q=VᵀPV, a column for the unordered pair (i,j) factors into the temporal vector at μ=λ_iλ_j and the values of the monomial z_i z_j on the actual starts. Time zero handles μ=0. With H≥s, distinct μ give independent temporal Vandermonde columns, so a left inverse separates the classes and the total rank is the sum of their ranks. Each is bounded by min(r,m_μ). The stated b_i make each unordered b_i b_j distinct: off-diagonal sums of two distinct binary powers have two bits, whereas diagonal sums carry to distinct one-bit exponents. Taking z_i^(k)=b_i^k supplies ordinary Vandermonde blocks and all of them attain their bounds simultaneously. This proves a maximum, not a statement for all starts. A nonzero polynomial minor gives the asserted genericity for absolutely continuous joint choices. Full rank is equivalent to r≥max m_μ. Below that, adding and subtracting a sufficiently small symmetric kernel vector from I gives two positive-definite alternatives. For the geometric family, each fixed index sum pairs disjoint indices with at most one diagonal pair; the maximum ceil(n/2) occurs at i+j=n+1, and the 2n−1 product values are distinct. Nonzero modal coordinates are cyclic for distinct eigenvalues by the ordinary Vandermonde, so n≥3 indeed separates ordinary cyclicity from quadratic identification. The supplied finite-field checker was inspected; the proof is over the reals and does not depend on it.

value.rationale: The sharp separate-trajectory requirement gives an experiment-design obstruction that more time cannot fix. Even stable distinct ordinary eigenvalues and a cyclic start may have product collisions; exhibiting exact attainability by genuine starts turns the multiplicity lower bound into a usable identifiability criterion. The result concerns noiseless unrestricted quadratic forms, not numerical conditioning or a shorter-horizon tradeoff.
